scenes.headline: How a network learns to take big molecular steps
scenes.sub: Langevin Flow Maps learn the integrator, not just the force
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jackstraw! Molecular dynamics crawls one femtosecond at a time. Here's how a network learns steps ten times bigger.

scenes.text: Train one network to predict the average velocity and force over a big step, given a summary of the noise along the way.
scenes.say: Don't just learn the force. Learn where the molecule ends up after a big step, given the random kicks along the way.

scenes.title: One big step
scenes.text: v_t = v_s - h(γ v_avg - f_avg/m) + σ ΔW
scenes.say: The update looks like the simplest integrator there is.

parts.note: force averaged along the true path, not at the start
parts.say: But the force is averaged along the true path, not taken at the start.
The velocity is averaged over the step too.

parts.note: the thermal kick, handed in explicitly
parts.say: And the thermal kick is sampled first and handed in.

scenes.title: One network call per big step

steps.say: A transformer reads the atoms, their velocities, and the step size.
It also reads four polynomial coefficients per atom that summarise the Brownian path over the step.
Two heads predict the averaged velocity and the averaged force.
One update jumps to the next state, up to ten femtoseconds later.

items.text: Sample a conformer and its forces
items.say: Take a single conformer and its forces.
Draw velocities at the target temperature.
At a zero step, the force head must match the true force.
And one big step must land where two half steps land, on the same path.

steps.say: A smooth polynomial summarises the grey Brownian path.
From it, the flow map jumps velocity and position onto the fine path.

scenes.title: The usual way and this one

left.title: BAOAB integrator
left.say: The usual integrator: about one femtosecond per force call.

right.title: Langevin Flow Map
right.say: The flow map: up to ten, but it needs a temperature corrector.

scenes.title: Alanine dipeptide, picoseconds per minute
scenes.note: same network, ten times the step
scenes.say: On alanine dipeptide, that is ten times the same network as a force field, and level with classical dynamics.

scenes.text: Learning the integral of the forces buys bigger steps; the sampler is only as good as the fit.
scenes.say: Learning the integral of the forces buys bigger steps. The sampler is only as good as the fit.

recap: Learn averaged velocity and force over a step
Hand the network the Brownian path
Train on half steps, not trajectories
scenes.say: Average over the step, hand in the noise, and train on half steps.
